parameter_reviews.name: envelope.pore_radius

declaration.source: radius of the NPC's passive-diffusion channel, ~9 nm diameter — the literature figure quoted in INVENTORY-2026-09-21 E' P1 and in language.BOUNDED_OMISSIONS['envelope_pores'] before this lane built the mechanism. Not read in a paper by this session and not in KB source_audit — EXAMPLE, register before SOURCED. Poiseuille with this radius and bulk water is a conductance CEILING: the FG-nucleoporin mesh inside the channel only adds resistance.

source_cards.title: Nuclear envelope permeability
source_cards.observational_unit: Nuclear-envelope sieving inferred from dextran passage
source_cards.finding: The reported patent radius is about 45 Å, equivalent to 4.5 nm radius or 9 nm diameter. This is a functional sieving estimate.
source_cards.transfer_limitations: No measured water hydraulic radius or structural opening follows. Numerical agreement does not prove that the uncited inventory statement originated from this paper. Full methods and fitting uncertainty were not obtained.

source_cards.title: Permeability of single nuclear pores
source_cards.primary_anchor: Author-public full text: printed p219 Eqs7–8; p224 radius discussion; p225 conditional length discussion; p226 Table2

conditions.sample: Isolated Xenopus oocyte nuclei attached to porous filters
conditions.assay: OSTR; fluorescent dextrans approximately4,10,20 kDa; ≥40 kDa did not permeate in this assay
conditions.temperature: Assay temperature not established in inspected passages; no value inferred from unrelated cited article snippets
conditions.buffer: Oocyte mock buffer:140mM KCl,3mM MgCl2,10mM HEPES,pH7.2; fluorophore dextrans4g/L

source_cards.observational_unit: Membrane-patch fluorescence recovery; fitted rate histograms provide k1 (or k125), then probe-pair ratios infer radius and conditional length.
source_cards.finding: Radius is inferred first from two probes, independently of channel number or length. Length is then calculated using that radius and single-channel k1. Table2 has six radius estimates 4.4–6.1 nm and three lengths 43.0,49.8,40.8 nm. This is linked inference, not a joint radius–length fit.
source_cards.transfer_limitations: Restricted-diffusion cylinder and hard-sphere approximations do not establish independently measured geometry, a hydraulic radius, or MCF7 values. Table2 ranges span derived estimates and are not confidence intervals; they do not supply a current prior. Single-NPC k1 is inferred from rate-histogram peaks, not a directly isolated one-NPC time trace; Eq.8 also uses probe properties and filter-pore volume.

conditions.probes: 11 inert probes, Stokes radius0.67–2.85 nm in Fig3
conditions.temperature: Assay temperature not established in inspected passages

source_cards.observational_unit: Relative nuclear-entry rates normalized to a reference probe and fitted to channel-size models
source_cards.finding: A uniform-radius fit gives2.66 nm but misses large-probe behavior; heterogeneous radii fit better. Rate ratios cancel assumed common nuisance factors, so this fit does not identify absolute channel length or NPC water conductance.
source_cards.transfer_limitations: Probe shape, binding exclusions and permeabilized preparation matter. A mesh radius inferred from solute passage must not be substituted for hydraulic radius. Competing diffusion models are retained; none is selected here.

source_cards.primary_anchor: Results first paragraph/Fig. 1A–C; Methods live microscopy and image analysis; BioC passages9–10,29,33

conditions.cell_cycle: Individual cells tracked mitosis to mitosis; earlyG1 versus lateG2
conditions.sampling: Images every1–2h; n=11 for density comparison

source_cards.observational_unit: Detected NPC fluorescence peaks / manually selected in-focus local nuclear-surface area
source_cards.finding: Density is 6.9±0.7 in earlyG1 and 6.4±0.8 in lateG2, in NPC/µm². Bottom and top densities were compared; bottom was assumed representative.

source_cards.title: The SUN protein UNC-84 is required only in force-bearing cells to maintain nuclear envelope architecture
source_cards.primary_anchor: Introduction; Fig. 1B,C/Fig. 2E; EM methods; BioC passages4,9,14,44

conditions.sample: C. elegans embryos/L1 larvae; wild type and unc-84 mutants
conditions.preparation: High-pressure freezing, freeze substitution;70nm serial TEM sections
conditions.measurement: Calibrated image distances; muscle analysis uses widest separation across serial sections

source_cards.observational_unit: Local membrane separation; maximum-per-nucleus in muscle analysis
source_cards.finding: About 50 nm spacing is described in wild-type embryonic/larval nuclei. Wild-type muscle maximum separations span 46.2–106.8nm, mean 68.1nm. The introduction’s 30–50 nm statement cites prior work.
source_cards.transfer_limitations: The maximum-per-nucleus statistic is not the typical lumen width. Neither is a cell-independent 40 nm constant, code radial scale offset, or pore hydraulic length. Membrane edge versus midplane conventions were not resolved in the inspected measurement description.

source_cards.observational_unit: Volume-versus-temperature curves jointly fitted for reference permeability and activation energy
source_cards.finding: Lpg and activation energy are jointly fitted per cooling rate. HTML Table 2 lists coefficients 0.430, 0.472, 0.306 and energies 239, 184, 103 kJ/mol. The retrieved HTML permeability header reads 10^13 m³/(N·s), with no minus sign.

source_cards.observational_unit: Initial normalized volume-response amplitude/rate combined with membrane surface area
source_cards.finding: The protocol uses Pf=k*C*V0/(Δc*A*Vw), with Vw=1.8×10^-5m³/mol. It warns that unknown membrane folds/ruffles make absolute Pf crude; relative rates alone are insufficient.

source_cards.finding: Pf is derived from shrinkage rate divided by area/volume, Vw and concentration difference; Vw=18cm³/mol. Lipid composition and channel density change measured permeability.

source_cards.primary_anchor: Methods/Fig. 2; Results reflection coefficients; Fig. 3/Table 1; Discussion early flux window

conditions.measurement: Initial5–10s volume slopes; typically20mM osmolyte changes; native membrane contribution corrected
conditions.reference: Impermeant mannitol for AQP1; sucrose/raffinose for AQP9

source_cards.observational_unit: Osmotic efficiency for a test solute relative to impermeant-reference Pf in the same oocyte
source_cards.finding: The measured efficiency is σPf. AQP1 tested-solute σ values cluster near 1; other channel/solute combinations differ. The reference osmolyte itself must be impermeant for that channel.
source_cards.transfer_limitations: A solute-specific ratio at 20–25°C is not a universal membrane constant or an NPC result. The study’s paired observations do not establish covariance or labels for the current global sigma 1 row.

relations.title: Passive diffusion estimates and hydraulic-radius mismatch
relations.expression: Paine:45 angstrom radius ->4.5nm radius ->9nm diameter; Keminer:probe-pair rate ratio ->equivalent radius, then radius plus single-channel k1 ->conditional equivalent length; Mohr:relative entry-rate model comparison
relations.qualification: Distinct experiments and model quantities. No automatic equality with r_hydraulic, no current shared-fit membership, no empirical covariance. The exact source chain of the inventory9nm phrase remains unresolved. Keminer Eqs7–8 are sequential conditional derivations, not a joint radius–length fit.

Triangle areas summed into initial area0.

relations.title: Conditional shell spacing and pore-length guard
relations.expression: R_inner=R_outer-spacing; with shared WrinkleField f(dir), radial vertex separation=spacing*f(dir); separately pore_length>=spacing

code_anchors.interpretation: Conditional inner sheet uses smaller radius, matched topology and same wrinkle field.
WrinkleField radii multiply nominal surface radius.
Pore-length lower bound compares declared scalars only.

relations.qualification: A radial scale difference is not generally local normal lumen width, bilayer-midplane separation or fitted diffusion length. The water law refuses the double-sheet branch; these are separate conditional code paths, not a measured simultaneous construction.

relations.title: Conditional Poiseuille conductance and area conversion

code_anchors.interpretation: Bare-cylinder formula, positivity/coverage/length guards and density multiplication.

relations.qualification: Extension of historical pore_hydraulic_geometry, not a newly independent finding. Single-pore docstring has areal units; dimensional algebra gives um^5. A real-water upper-bound claim needs matched hydraulic geometry/no-slip/bulk-viscosity assumptions; a solute-equivalent radius does not establish it. No actual NPC water flux is measured.

relations.title: Pf to hydraulic Lp with matched area and temperature

code_anchors.interpretation: Reference temperature checks pressure-per-mM conversion; runtime pressure uses actual kBT, not a Pf conversion.
Membrane Lp is read as an input; envelope Lp comes from pore geometry.

relations.qualification: Definition conversion only, assuming the same T, surface-area convention, ideal concentration driving force and correctly treated reflection. Pf is osmotic permeability, not diffusional Pd or single-channel Pu. With an unknown permeant osmolyte, a shrinkage-only estimate can confound sigma*Pf; no universal conversion of fitted assay rate alone. The flux equality compares a consistently signed driving concentration difference at zero hydrostatic pressure difference.

algebraic_example_not_measurement.temperature_note: 310 K is the frozen declared reference, not exactly 310.15 K. Do not reuse a Pf measured at another T without an experimentally supported temperature relation.

relations.title: Reflection coefficient is a boundary-solute scope restriction

code_anchors.interpretation: Osmotic pressure from fixed pool counts and water volumes.
Rejects any reflection value different from1.
One declared global reflection row passed to plasma and nuclear surfaces.

relations.qualification: The code variable sigma elsewhere is the signed pool-incidence matrix, not this reflection coefficient. sigma1 is not a direct universal biological measurement; source osmolyte/channel ratios cannot be copied across boundaries. No ion/permeant-solute mechanism is chosen.

declaration.source: SWITCH, not a measurement: 1 binds cell/transport_build -> physics/surface_transport (face law q = n.(Vv - Ju), R = A/Lp, Pi = kBT(Nin/Vin - Nout/Vout) from the enclosed geometry). 0 = the shipped build, unchanged. With 1, membrane.pressure must be 0.0 (the declared turgor becomes the comparison target, not a second load) and StepConfig.fluid_volume_consistent must be false (this law replaces that numerical correction).

switch: 1 builds the inner sheet at envelope.spacing inside the outer one and ties them one-to-one. DEFAULT 0 = the single-sheet build, tables bit-identical. not in KB source_audit — register before SOURCED

water at 37 C, 0.692 mPa.s (CRC Handbook; 1.002 is the 20 C value, which stood here as 'water at 37 C' until 2026-09-21). One fluid grid serves inside and outside the cell, so this is water at the stage temperature; composite cytoplasm viscosity is an OUTPUT (directive 9). laws/units.ETA_SOLVENT still holds the old literal. PARAMETERS-2026-09-21

the declared reference of the unit conversion, not a biological parameter: osmotic.pressure_per_mM is R x this temperature (8.314 x 310 = 2577 Pa/mM), checked at build. Runtime pressure uses the actual kBT and molecule counts, so changing cell.temperature does not freeze RT here.
